body:
What reached me is the account and the rival; the objection view is absent from what was passed to me. That absence tells me only that nothing arrived in this view — not that either artifact survived an independent critical pass, and not that one failed. Both carry their own embedded objections (the account's worry that it over-reads ambiguity, the rival's worry that its reading can pathologize ordinary explicitness), so the critical function is partially but only internally served. My synthesis inherits that unexercised surface, and I will flag where I most want a critic to push.

The central decision is easier than it looks, because the two readings do not force a choice of opening move. The rival's test — watch whether the avoiding flatmate engages with a proposal's content or pulls back from the proposal itself — can only be run after some proposal exists. It is operationally parasitic on the account's move. So 'start with the note' versus 'start with the household question' partly dissolves: the sequence can be concrete conversations first, then a minimal note, with the reaction instrumented. I use the account's ladder and the rival's diagnostic rather than choosing between them.

From the account I keep: the smallest recurring items rather than a general fairness talk, low ceremony (a fridge note or a shared thread, explicitly a draft), the three columns including the fallback clause, and the one-to-one approach with a narrow ask. From the rival I keep: the second axis, the reaction test, truce-shaped arrangements as a fallback, and the instruction to keep separate conversations separate rather than aggregating them into a group decision.

What I revise is the rival's opening move. Posing 'is this flat a shared unit or three private lives?' directly is a high-stakes framing question, and high-stakes framing questions are exactly the genre being avoided. It also risks converting a chore dispute into a household-ideology dispute — the same failure shape as the account's warning about specification problems becoming character disputes. The revision: ask the question obliquely. The fallback hypothetical carries it: 'if you can't do your turn because of work, what do you think should happen?' An answer like 'tell us and we'll cover it' expresses something close to a unit reading; bristling at 'your turn' expresses something closer to the privacy reading. If concrete conversations never surface any meta-level disagreement, that is itself evidence against the rival reading for this household — so the revision tests the rival rather than suppressing it.

Two convergences raise my confidence where the artifacts agree despite different diagnoses. Both end at the same escalation boundary: if low-pressure attempts fail, stop optimizing chores and name the living-arrangement question. And both, in different vocabularies, aim to reduce live negotiation — the account's fallback column and the rival's default outcomes are the same instinct twice. Independent arrival is weak evidence, but real; those components survive even if either diagnosis proves wrong.

Before running anything I would pre-commit the branch rules, because this household's characteristic failure is reinterpreting agreements after the fact, and an experiment can be reinterpreted the same way. Content-engagement plus falling recurrence: continue the specification track. Pullback from the proposal's form itself: switch to a truce-shaped arrangement — owned zones, or a rotation with a default nobody negotiates in the moment — without re-litigating the note. Truce also declined: name the living-arrangement question explicitly. Rules decided in advance are the anti-ambiguity medicine applied to the experiment itself. And neither signal is decisive alone: recurrence can fall because of attention rather than specification, and a single pullback can reflect busyness or discomfort with writing things down rather than rejection of obligation. The branches get read with error bars and never reported to anyone as a verdict about anyone.

Two cautions I have to raise myself, since no independent objection arrived to raise them. First, the reaction test, done too deliberately, treats a friend as a diagnostic object; the mitigation is transparency — say 'I don't know what arrangement fits us; let's try something small for two weeks and see' rather than presenting the note as a solution. Second, complexity: the combined plan must stay small in practice — week one is two short conversations and one fridge-note item. If even that cannot be executed, that is a finding about the household, not only a failure of the plan.

One reserve move neither artifact tries, because both are talk-first. If the one-to-one ask is also declined, try arrangement-first: take over the single most recurring item unilaterally for a defined fortnight, note it neutrally, present no invoice, then disclose afterward and ask whether it should continue. This tests whether the avoidance is about being asked to negotiate at all. The risk is genuine — silent over-covering hides imbalance and breeds resentment — so it is time-boxed, disclosed, and never a standing pattern; it belongs just before the living-arrangement conversation, not before the probe.

What stays open: the cause of the avoidance. Nothing in the material distinguishes conflict fatigue, perceived load imbalance, aversion to being bound, or stress with nothing to do with the flat, and only the probes can close that, slowly. What I reject outright: only the framing that the two readings force a choice of opening move. Everything else here is use, revision, or deliberately left open.

this records only that nothing arrived, not that either survived criticism.","scope":"The unexercised critical surface of this synthesis.","consequence":"The untested vulnerabilities most worth pressing are whether any talk-based apparatus fits a household tired of talking (partially answered by k9, not resolved) and whether the branch rules in k5 can be misread or gamed under stress.","mentions":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#o1","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r9"]}],"uptake":["k1","k2","k3","k4","k5","k6","k7","k8","k9","k10","k11"]}
